title: Molanus of Louvain likewise defends carrying images in processions, setting them on altars, and clothing them in gold and precious garments
source_text: XIX. Similia videre est apud Joannem Molanum Theologum Lovaniensem, qui in libro de historia sacrarum Imaginum, earum publicam circumgestationem, & positionem super altaria, studiumque illas vestibus pretiosis ornandi, tuetur & propugnat. Nam libro secundo capitis trigesimi quarti, lemma est, Imaginum in supplicationibus circumgestatio a superstitione contra haereticos defenditur. Et tricesimi noni capitis titulus est Sanctorum imaginibus non profane & Ethnice, sed religiose altaria exornari. Sequentis vero capitis, Imagines Sanctorum recte auro & argento tegi, & coronis, vel pretiosis vestibus exornari.
pass_a_gloss: Similar things may be seen in John Molanus, Louvain theologian, who in his book on the history of sacred Images defends and champions their public carrying-about, their placement upon altars, and the zeal for adorning them with precious garments. For in the second book, of the thirty-fourth chapter, the lemma is, The carrying of Images in processions is defended from superstition against heretics. And of the thirty-ninth chapter the title is, Altars are adorned with the images of the Saints not profanely and Ethnically, but religiously. And of the following chapter, The Images of the Saints are rightly covered with gold and silver, and adorned with crowns or precious garments.
pass_b_english: Louvain’s Molanus champions processions, altar-images, and gold-and-garment adornment against the ‘superstition’ charge.

choices.why: Roman apologetic for the full public cultus.
